target_customer: HR and learning leaders at mid-market and enterprise employers who buy coaching for managers and executives
problem: Executive and leadership coaching was expensive, hard to scale and hard to measure, so most managers never got it.
business_model: B2B subscription and per-coaching-engagement fees paid by employers, with coaches paid per session

founders.name: Cameron Yarbrough
prior_employers: Stanford Graduate School of Business (leadership facilitator)
previous_startups: A prior company where he grew a team of 50+ psychologists and psychotherapists (name not given on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he practiced clinical psychology and has Vipassana meditation training. Education not listed.

founders.name: Keegan Walden
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder on the YC page and in the 2019 TechCrunch article. Later became a founder coach.

competitors.name: BetterUp
competitors.what: Mobile coaching platform bringing coaching to employees at all levels
competitors.traction_then: Used by Fortune 500 companies per its own release

technical_complexity.rationale: A matching and measurement platform on top of human coaches. Standard web engineering with no hard research problem.

defensibility.rationale: Coach network and employer data gave some stickiness, but coaching platforms were easy to copy and compete on service quality.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought Torch. It grew into a consolidator itself, merging with Everwise in early 2020 and buying Praxis Labs in July 2025.

market_need_then: Employers spent heavily on executive coaching for a few leaders only. The 2019 TechCrunch article describes about 100 clients including Reddit and Atrium, which shows demand for coaching beyond the C-suite.

branding.domain_note: Uses torch.io, a .io domain rather than an exact .com. Acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Not described by any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident, for example the line Experienced leaders. Worth your leaders' time, on the company site

branding.brand_signature: Tagline Leadership coaching, reimagined, per a listing of the company's logo page

rebrands.why: Combined with Everwise under the Torch brand, per a search snippet of a 2020 announcement

brand_strength.rationale: Plain, generic name shared with many companies. No mascot or community found. The brand carried the company in enterprise sales but no source shows it as a growth driver.

outcome_analysis: Torch was listed as Inactive by the YC directory, but sources show it kept operating: it raised a Series A in 2019, a $25M Series B in 2021 and a $40M Series C in 2022, merged with Everwise in 2020 and acquired Praxis Labs in July 2025. Its enterprise coaching sales motion found demand from employers wanting to scale coaching to managers. The Inactive label looks like a directory error or a rename, so this record is not a failure case.
notes: YC directory status Inactive conflicts with evidence of active operation through 2026. Series A amount varies by source: TechCrunch says $10M; databases say $6.5M or $12.4M. Seed round rests on a single database (CB Insights) with no amount. Series C rests on the YC page and a search summary of press coverage. Reported totals range from about $43.9M to $87.8M; the recorded rounds sum to $75M plus an undisclosed seed, so the gap is small but unresolved. Series B blog says nearly $40M total including that round, which conflicts with the recorded earlier rounds. Education of both founders not found.
